items.title: Frank Alkyer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Orleans, Louisiana, January 10, 2020
items.q: this guy named Benny Goodman, this kid became an overnight sensation across the country... That became DownBeat’s reason to be, covering Benny Goodman

ctx.x: I didn’t know I made a joke.

Well in 1934 there was no mission statement believe you me. You know the first issue I think was eight pages long and it was basically a listing of all the bands and where they were playing and who was in the bands, because the guy who started the magazine sold life insurance policies to the — he was also a saxophone player on the side — but he sold life insurance. And he wanted to keep track of his clients. So DownBeat started as a little newsletter for this guy who sold life insurance. So there was not much of…

journalists, they were musicians mostly. They were cantankerous, they were, you know it was, there was some funny stuff that would go on. And I wish that we could do some of that. And sometimes we try to get an element of it, but we just can’t be quite that freewheeling when you’re 85 years old and you’ve been around for all this time. We have a little bit more weight and gravitas that we need to present in the magazine, so —
